correctness.rationale: Couple the two distinct focal sampling pools by swapping the other focal individual. When that individual is drawn, both groups have the same cooperator count; otherwise the count difference is the unit increment of j·1{j≥M} in the common Z−2 pool. This gives the factor (Z−N)/(Z−1) and the stated H. Coupling adjacent compositions by recoloring one background individual gives the difference of the two adjacent hypergeometric masses at M−2 and M−1. Factoring the binomials gives the sign of MZ−N(k+1) wherever M−1≤k≤Z−N+M−1; outside this interval both relevant masses are zero. The root lies strictly inside this interval, including the case Z=N+1. This proves the mode and adjacent tie rule, H(1)=0, H(Z−1)=1 and H_*>1. Strict upper level sets are consecutive, empty at or below Fcrit, with precisely the mode(s) neutral at equality. Fcrit is the infimum, not an attained minimum for strict advantage. The sign on the right endpoint changes at Ftail, and both extremes are negative with a positive intermediate band for Fcrit<F<Ftail (zeros at interfaces do not add sign reversals). The claim concerns drift sign under positive Fermi comparison intensity, not fixation or extra absorbing states. Separate-pool exact rational checks implemented independently for 4≤Z≤15 passed 4,095 payoff comparisons, 3,731 adjacent-difference comparisons and the mode checks; verify.py and its recorded results were inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: An exact finite mode and threshold fill a natural gap between separate hypergeometric payoff sums, simulations and the infinite-population analogue. The values identify the compositions most favorable to cooperation without scanning all compositions, distinguish the first possible positive drift from positive drift at the high endpoint, and capture a finite-size suppression and exact tie that a continuous approximation misses. The result does not imply fixation behavior.
